description: What no check covers, why, who reviews it, in which review and when. Every entry needs all five; an entry missing one fails the residual-judgement-register check. Add an entry whenever you find something a check cannot see that someone must still judge.

entries.what: Whether each module boundary is in the right place
entries.whyNotChecked: The check enforces the boundaries in the module map; no tool knows the business's language well enough to say where they should be
entries.reviewer: A design reviewer who knows the domain
entries.when: On every change that adds, splits or merges a module, or adds a line to the module map

entries.what: Whether each event field is marked correctly as identifying a person or not, and whether each event type's retention period is one the organisation may keep
entries.whyNotChecked: The test holds events to the contract; it cannot tell what a field means or what the law allows
entries.reviewer: The owner of the data, with the organisation's data protection officer
entries.review: Review of the change to the telemetry contract
entries.when: On every change that adds an event type or a field to the telemetry contract

entries.what: Whether a package on the dependency allowlist is safe to use
entries.whyNotChecked: The allowlist check is a policy check: it says whether a package was approved, not whether it is safe
entries.reviewer: The rule's owner, who approves the entry
entries.review: Review of the change that adds the allowlist entry
